'''Jacob Tsimerman'''{{efn|{{langx|ru|Яков Цимерман|translit=Yakov Tsimerman
}}, {{Langx|he|ג'ייקוב צימרמן|translit=Jakov Tzimarman}}}} (born April 26, 1988) is an [[Israelis|Israeli]]-[[Soviet Union|Soviet]]-born Canadian mathematician at the [[University of Toronto]] specialising in [[arithmetic geometry]], [[algebraic geometry]], and related areas. He was awarded the [[SASTRA Ramanujan Prize]] in the year 2015 in recognition for his work on the [[André–Oort conjecture]] and for his work in both [[analytic number theory]] and [[algebraic geometry]].<ref name=Princeton>{{cite web|title=Jacob Tsimerman Awarded 2015 SASTRA Ramanujan Prize|url=https://www.math.princeton.edu/news/home-page/jacob-tsimerman-11-awarded-2015-sastra-ramanujan-prize|publisher=Princeton University|access-date=November 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170324015411/http://www.math.princeton.edu/news/home-page/jacob-tsimerman-11-awarded-2015-sastra-ramanujan-prize|archive-date=March 24, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2026, he received the [[Fields Medal]] for his work on [[O-minimality]], Griffiths' conjecture,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Bakker | first1=Benjamin | last2=Brunebarbe | first2=Yohan | last3=Tsimerman | first3=Jacob | title=o-minimal GAGA and a conjecture of Griffiths | journal=Inventiones mathematicae | volume=232 | issue=1 | date=2023 | issn=0020-9910 | doi=10.1007/s00222-022-01166-1 | pages=163–228 | url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00222-022-01166-1 | access-date=2026-07-29| url-access=subscription }}</ref> and the André–Oort conjecture.<ref name=":0" />

== Early life and education ==
Tsimerman was born on April 26, 1988 in [[Kazan]], Soviet Union.<ref name="AMS" /> In 1990, his family moved to [[Israel]] and then in 1996 to Canada.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |date=2026-07-23 |title=Jacob Tsimerman Lives in Number Theory |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/23/science/jacob-tsimerman-fields-medal.html |access-date=2026-07-26 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> He attended the [[University of Toronto Schools]] for high school, where he represented Canada in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] in 2003 and 2004, winning gold medals both times with a perfect score in 2004.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=7387 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120505013514/http://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=7387 |archive-date=May 5, 2012 |title=Jacob Tsimerman – IMO results }}</ref><ref name="Sasaki">{{cite news |last1=Sasaki |first1=Chris |title='Nobel Prize of mathematics': U of T mathematician Jacob Tsimerman awarded prestigious Fields Medal |url=https://www.utoronto.ca/news/nobel-prize-mathematics-u-t-mathematician-jacob-tsimerman-awarded-prestigious-fields-medal |publisher=U of T News |date=July 23, 2026 |archive-date=July 23, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723164058/https://www.utoronto.ca/news/nobel-prize-mathematics-u-t-mathematician-jacob-tsimerman-awarded-prestigious-fields-medal |url-status=live }}</ref>

Tsimerman began his post-secondary studies at [[University College, Toronto|University College]], [[University of Toronto]], at the age of 16, where he graduated after two years in 2006 with a bachelor's degree in mathematics.<ref name="Sasaki"/><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Rinaldi |first=Luc |date=July 16, 2026 |title=Locked in an escape room with mathematician Jacob Tsimerman |url=https://www.begiant.ca/stories/people/jacob-tsimerman-math |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=www.begiant.ca |language=en |archive-date=July 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723165838/https://www.begiant.ca/stories/people/jacob-tsimerman-math |url-status=live }}</ref> He obtained his PhD from [[Princeton University|Princeton]] in 2011<ref>{{Cite web|date=October 1, 2019|title=Impressive breakthroughs by U of T's youngest faculty member in math, Jacob Tsimerman {{!}} Faculty of Arts & Science|url=https://www.artsci.utoronto.ca/news/impressive-breakthroughs-u-ts-youngest-faculty-member-math-jacob-tsimerman|access-date=October 21, 2021|archive-date=October 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001222921/https://www.artsci.utoronto.ca/news/impressive-breakthroughs-u-ts-youngest-faculty-member-math-jacob-tsimerman|url-status=live}}</ref> under the guidance of [[Peter Sarnak]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jacob Tsimerman|url=http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=184290|access-date=November 8, 2015|publisher=Mathematics Genealogy Project|archive-date=July 7, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200707221604/https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=184290|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Career ==
Following his PhD, he had a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral]] position at [[Harvard University]] as a Junior Fellow of the Harvard Society of Fellows. In July 2014, he was awarded a [[Sloan Fellowship]], and he started his term as assistant professor in the [[Department of Mathematics (University of Toronto)|Department of Mathematics]] at the University of Toronto, where he is now a full professor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.utoronto.ca/~jacobt/|title=Jacob Tsimerman|website=www.math.utoronto.ca|access-date=July 24, 2026|archive-date=July 24, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260724062853/https://www.math.utoronto.ca/~jacobt/|url-status=live}}</ref> 

In 2018, Tsimerman was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] (ICM).<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU) |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Tsimerman |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=www.mathunion.org |archive-date=May 19, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240519121927/https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=Tsimerman |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2019, he was awarded the [[Coxeter–James Prize]] by the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Coxeter-James Prize – CMS-SMC |url=https://cms.math.ca/awards/coxeter-james-prize/ |access-date=May 19, 2024 |language=en-US |archive-date=May 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240513144331/https://cms.math.ca/awards/coxeter-james-prize/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He is also one of winners of the 2022 New Horizons in Mathematics Prize, associated with the [[Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics]]. He was awarded for "outstanding work in analytic number theory and arithmetic geometry, including breakthroughs on the André-Oort and Griffiths conjectures".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Breakthrough Prize – Mathematics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – Jacob Tsimerman |url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3910 |access-date=May 19, 2024 |website=breakthroughprize.org |language=en |archive-date=May 16, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240516232402/https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3910 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2023, Tsimerman received the [[Ostrowski Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ostrowski |url=https://www.ostrowski.ch/index_e.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240516232408/https://www.ostrowski.ch/index_e.php |archive-date=May 16, 2024 |website=ostrowski.ch}}</ref> 
In 2024, he was awarded the [[John L. Synge Award]] from the [[Royal Society of Canada]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Number theory scholar, Jacob Tsimerman, receives prestigious John L. Synge Award from the Royal Society of Canada|url=https://www.artsci.utoronto.ca/news/number-theory-scholar-jacob-tsimerman-receives-prestigious-john-l-synge-award-royal-society|access-date=2026-09-03|website=www.artsci.utoronto.ca}}</ref>
He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 20, 2025 |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |access-date=May 22, 2025 |website=Royal Society |language=en |archive-date=November 8, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251108103819/https://royalsociety.org/news/2025/05/new-fellows/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Between 2025 and 2026, Tsimerman was a visiting professor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 20, 2023 |title=Jacob Tsimerman {{!}} Scholars {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/jacob-tsimerman |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=www.ias.edu |language=en |archive-date=July 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723165923/https://www.ias.edu/scholars/jacob-tsimerman |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2026, Tsimerman was awarded the [[Fields Medal]] at ICM Philadelphia 2026 for his "contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the André-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties."<ref name=":0">{{cite web | title=Fields Medals 2026 | website=www.mathunion.org | url=https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-2026 | access-date=July 23, 2026 | archive-date=July 23, 2026 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723135714/https://www.mathunion.org/imu-awards/fields-medal/fields-medals-2026 | url-status=live }}</ref> He became the first faculty member at a Canadian university to win the Fields Medal.<ref>{{cite news|last=Lewis|first=Stewart|date=2026-07-24 |url=https://nationalpost.com/news/canada/u-of-t-math-professor-is-first-scholar-at-a-canadian-university-to-win-prestigious-fields-medal |title=U of T math professor is first scholar at a Canadian university to win prestigious Fields Medal |work=National Post|access-date=2026-08-13}}</ref> There, he announced he was joining [[OpenAI]] as a researcher in [[AI safety]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cohen |first=Ben |date=2026-08-01 |title=The Math Superstar Who’s Terrified of AI—and Just Took a Job at OpenAI |url=https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/openai-jacob-tsimerman-fields-medal-ai-safety-391d0f79 |access-date=2026-08-02 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/this-u-of-t-professor-just-won-maths-highest-honour--and-is-taking-a-leave-to-join-openai-heres-why/article_cee2c80f-9ea1-47f7-ad4d-8f3d76bbb0a2.html</ref>

==Research==
Together with [[Jonathan Pila]], Tsimerman demonstrated the [[André–Oort conjecture]] for [[Siegel modular form|Siegel modular varieties]].  Later, he completed the proof of the André–Oort conjecture for the [[Shimura variety]] by reducing the problem to the [[Colmez conjecture|averaged Colmez conjecture]] which was proved by [[Xinyi Yuan]] and [[Shou-Wu Zhang]] as well as independently by Andreatta, Goren, Howard and Madapusi-Pera.<ref name="AMS">{{cite journal |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |title=Tsimerman Receives Aisenstadt Prize |issn=1088-9477 |volume=65 |issue=2 |year= |page=191 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201802/rnoti-p191.pdf |date=February 2018 |archive-date=January 6, 2026 |access-date=July 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106195249/https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201802/rnoti-p191.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2021, Tsimerman, Pila and [[Ananth Shankar]] published a full proof of the André–Oort conjecture.<ref name=":1" />
